How to build a bird box

Building a bird box is one of the simplest woodworking projects you can do in a weekend, and the birds in your garden will thank you for it when spring arrives and they are looking for somewhere safe to nest.

You need one plank of untreated pine, about fifteen centimetres wide and one and a half metres long, a handful of galvanised screws, a drill, a saw and a pencil. Avoid treated timber, because the chemicals can harm the chicks.

Mark the plank into six pieces: the front, the back, the two sides, the roof and the base. The back should be longer than the front so that the roof slopes and the rain runs off, which keeps the nest dry through the wettest weeks of April.

Drill a hole of twenty-five millimetres in the front for blue tits, or thirty-two millimetres for house sparrows, and put it at least twelve centimetres above the base so that cats cannot reach in. Read more in our guide to hole sizes.

Screw the pieces together, fix the box to a wall or tree two to four metres up, facing between north and east, and leave it alone. Clean it out each autumn once the birds have gone, and it will last for many years.
